subject: Dedicated GPU lane — budget anchor, throughput targets, and next steps
messages:
From: Samira Patel <s.patel@valence.ai>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Briggs <tom.b@valence.ai>, procurement@valence.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: throughput & budget after demo

Thanks for the demo today, Diego — good session. A quick recap from our side and what we need to move this forward: 

- Target workload: real-time classification + short summaries for customer messages. Median request = 420 tokens, 95th = 1,200 tokens.
- Average traffic expected: 12M tokens/day initially (spiky), target 40M tokens/day in 6 months during ramp.
- Latency SLO: 150–250ms p95 for median requests; for >1k token requests we can tolerate 350–500ms.
- Hard budget band: $10k–$45k/month for committed capacity in year 1.

We want a price anchor and suggested reserved lane sizing (GPU family + count) that will hit ~40M tokens/day while keeping p95 under 300ms for median requests. Also tell us expected $/1M tokens for the configurations you recommend and a 30/60/90-day pilot option.

Can you send a short commercial anchor (banded options) and the throughput assumptions used? Procurement wants a one‑page SOW to start procurement review.

Thanks — Samira
Samira Patel
Head of ML Ops, Valence AI
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Samira Patel <s.patel@valence.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: throughput & budget after demo

Samira — thanks for the clear recap. Below is a concise post‑call qualification and three banded options (pilot → production) that align to your traffic and latency goals. Attached: Redwood_Dedicated_Price_Options.pdf and a short throughput estimate.

Quick notes about assumptions used:
- Median request = 420 tokens, average token length = 4 chars, token generation ratio ~1:1 for summaries.
- 40M tokens/day ≈ sustained 463 tokens/sec (24/7). We model bursts up to 6x sustained for peak windows.
- p95 latency target measured on a 512-token workspace for each GPU family; we include continuous batching and KV cache hits for repeated prefixes.

Option A — Pilot (30–60 days):
- Hardware: 1x A100‑80GB (reserved lane) + autoscale headroom to 2x for sustained bursts.
- Throughput: modeled ~1.2–1.8k tokens/sec (batched) for median requests, expected p95 ~220–300ms.
- Unit price estimate: $18–$25 per 1M tokens (pilot configuration + premium pilot support).
- Commit: month-to-month pilot fee (recommended $12k–$18k/mo).

Option B — Starter Reserved (production initial):
- Hardware: 2x A100‑80GB reserved lanes (primary) + 4x L4 for lower-cost fanout for short prompts.
- Throughput: combined modeled ~5–7k tokens/sec sustained, handles 40M tokens/day comfortably with burst headroom. p95 ~180–260ms for median.
- Unit price estimate: $9–$13 per 1M tokens (depends on batching effectiveness and percent cache hit).
- Commit: 6–12 month reserved capacity; suggested anchor $40k–$70k/mo.

Option C — High-throughput committed (scale):
- Hardware: 4x H100 or mixed H100 + A100 lanes (we’ll right‑size based on final perf tests).
- Throughput: modeled >12k tokens/sec sustained; p95 <200ms for median.
- Unit price estimate: $5–$9 per 1M tokens (best unit economics, longer commit).
- Commit: 12+ months; commercial anchors start at $120k/mo.

Notes on tradeoffs: A100 lanes give better price/perf for mixed workloads; H100 favors very high throughput at lower $/1M but requires longer commitments. L4s are excellent for shallow, high‑fanout calls to reduce cost on simple prompts.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Confirm which option (A/B/C) aligns to Valence procurement appetite.
2) We can run a 2‑day perf test on your sample dataset (you provide a 1k-request replay) — we’ll deliver measured p50/p95, tokens/sec, and a refined $/1M projection.
3) I’ll send a one‑page SOW template and a banded quote for the selected option.

I’m looping Ben to kick off commercial and Laura for implementation scheduling.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Samira Patel <s.patel@valence.ai>, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU lane — budget anchor, throughput targets, and next steps

Samira — appreciate the clarity. A couple commercial checkpoints from my side before we draft SOW: 

- Procurement threshold: does Valence need a PO for pilot spend > $10k? If so we’ll structure pilot as an initial invoiceable deposit or short term reservation.
- Preferred billing cadence: monthly or quarterly? We typically recommend monthly for pilots and quarterly for multi‑lane commits.
- Discount triggers: 6–12 month committed lanes get stepped unit discounts; we can show exact $/1M for your final throughput after the perf test.

Attached is a one‑page SOW template (one_page_sow-template.docx). If you confirm pilot PO approach and billing cadence, I’ll get a draft SOW + banded quote to your procurement by EOD Wednesday.

Would you be open to a short procurement call Thursday 10am PT to confirm timing?

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Briggs <tom.b@valence.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: Samira Patel <s.patel@valence.ai>, procurement@valence.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU lane — budget anchor, throughput targets, and next steps

Thanks, team — this looks reasonable. Procurement: we can issue a PO for a $15k pilot deposit if Redwood will commit to a 2‑day perf run and a refined banded quote after. Monthly billing is preferred.

We’d like the perf run next week (Mon/Tue preferred). Please send the SOW and the perf test checklist so our infra and security folks can prep.

Tom
Tom Briggs
VP Engineering, Valence AI
